A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 35-page versions of the same LPW paper. The main text, equations, Tables 1–15, Figures 1–19, and Appendices A–G, including eight prompt listings, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original LPW benchmark experiments, ablations, cost analyses, and failure analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–3 and appendix investigations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Listings 1–8 retain the same two-phase LPW procedure: plan generation and verification, followed by code generation and iterative debugging using execution traces and error analysis.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven benchmarks, MBPP-ET-3 variant, and appendix scenarios. Correcting CodeContest to CodeContests in the abstract does not change the represented dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator membership: Baseline, Self-Planning, MapCoder, Self-Debugging, and LDB in the relevant tables, plus Repeated Sampling in the cost-performance comparisons.

E3.justification: The model configurations, two-shot prompting, iteration limits, Pass@1 metric, visible/hidden-test arrangements, and sample counts are unchanged. Appendix parameter studies and APPS/CodeContests preprocessing also retain their settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, iteration study, additional-visible-test analysis, cost-performance analyses, difficulty breakdowns, failure investigations, and case studies are retained with the same evidence in the main text and Appendices B–G.

E5.justification: Both versions specify standard deviations based on three runs in Table 1’s caption. The same uncertainty displays and stated omissions are retained throughout the tables and figures.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o LPW accuracies of 98.2% on HumanEval, 84.8% on MBPP, 59.3% on LiveCode, 62.6% on APPS, and 34.7% on CodeContests.

T1.justification: Section 2’s formal problem definition and Section 3’s verification conditions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about LPW, plan verification, and improved code-generation accuracy. The added code-access statement does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of plan verification, refinement efficiency, and failure mechanisms remain unchanged. Section 8 retains the limitations concerning imperfect LLM reasoning, substantial token consumption, and difficulty translating accurate plans into correct code.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit repository address and public-code statement to the abstract. v2 already referred readers to released code for complete prompts in Appendix G.4 and the listings, but supplied no repository address. This improves access documentation without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to planning, prompting, code refinement, and multi-agent approaches are unchanged. Reference text reflows across pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 updates an author’s email, adds the code-access sentence, corrects CodeContest to CodeContests in the abstract, and fixes HuamEval in two table headings. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 7 and 8 correct their HumanEval headings, slightly adjusting table widths and alignment. The abstract addition causes text reflow through the main paper. Figures, table structures, and their substantive visual contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The added repository address supplies a concrete access pointer for code and complete prompts already referenced in v2, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Benchmark-name corrections improve presentation consistency. The scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
